### Observed differences

- In the later window, A20, A28, A29 and A30 each occur about once in almost every trace — participation roughly 99 in 100 traces, against 0 to 1 of 200 traces in the earlier window. [OCC003, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009]
- Conversely, A19, A21, A22 and A23, each present in about 20 to 28 of 100 earlier traces (at most once per trace), drop to about 1 to 2 of 100 traces later. [OCC002, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006]
- A46's outgoing flow flips from the fading group to the new one: earlier, roughly 20 to 28 of 100 of its outgoing transitions went to each of A19, A21, A22 and A23; later, roughly 19 to 26 of 100 go to each of A20, A28, A29 and A30. [DIR011, DIR004, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]
- The earlier pattern around A14/A15 was a single pick: exactly one of A19/A21/A22/A23 per trace (pairs among them co-occur in at most about 1 of 200 traces), typically following A14/A15 and flowing on to A31 in about 25 to 28 of 100 traces. [REL024, REL025, REL040, REL030, REL045, DIR003, DIR007]
- In the later window, A14 precedes each of A20, A28, A29 and A30 in about 97 to 98 of 100 traces; the four co-occur in about 98 of 100 traces with no fixed order among themselves (either direction about 43 to 55 in 100); each precedes A31 in about 97 to 98 of 100 traces. A15 also co-occurs with the four, but with interleaving in about 44 of 100 traces. [REL010, REL013, REL015, REL035, REL056, REL038, REL063, REL017]
- The observed distance from A46 to A31 stretches from about 2 positions in 97 of 100 earlier pairs to the 5-step maximum in about 98 of 100 later pairs, consistent with four activities now sitting between them. [LAG003, REL039]
- A06 halves its footprint (about 27 to 14 of 100 traces), appears later within traces (median position about 0.17 to 0.28 of trace length), and its outgoing transitions spread from mostly A15 (about 89 of 100) to many targets (A15 about 43 of 100); it now usually runs without the new activities (co-occurrence about 13 of 100). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL002]
- The backbone is stable: A14, A15, A31 and A46 appear in every trace in both windows, with only small position shifts (A31 slightly later, mean about 0.40 to 0.46; A46, A14 and A15 slightly earlier). [POS002, POS003, POS012, POS013]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment running after A14/A15 and A46, and before A31, is executed differently in the later window: earlier traces contained a single activity chosen from A19, A21, A22 and A23 in that segment, while later traces instead run A20, A28, A29 and A30 there — each once, in varying order. About 100 evidence items qualify, against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [OCC003, DIR011, REL035, REL038, LAG003]

The support is direct rather than merely cumulative: the participation flip shows the old activities are no longer executed and the new ones now are; A46's rerouting and the A14-precedes relations locate the new activities between A46/A14 and A31; and the A46-to-A31 distance growing from about 2 to 5 positions matches four activities running where one did before. The old four behaved as mutually exclusive single picks, while the new four co-occur in the same traces. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR011, REL010, REL024, REL035, LAG003]

Limitations: the windows are finite samples, so an extreme shift in the mix of pre-existing variants cannot be strictly excluded — the new run simply not drawn in the 200 earlier traces and the old pick nearly not drawn later — although a behaviour at about 99 of 100 frequency appearing 0 times in 200 earlier traces makes that hard to sustain. Zero participation only means an activity was not observed, not that it was removed, and many items restate the same trace behaviour, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. [OCC003, OCC002, REL035]
